reasons: No tests are visible in the packet, although the comment says replays are reproducible for tests.
The rain check looks only for the presence of a method field.
Fake timings are used for both event time and observed time, which hides when the data was really recorded.

terms.meaning: A free public database of cricket match records.
A record that describes every single delivery in a match.
One ball bowled by the bowler to the batter.
A set of six legal balls bowled from one end.
One team's turn to bat in a match.
Runs not scored off the bat, such as wides, no-balls, byes and leg-byes.
A formula, Duckworth-Lewis, that resets the target score when rain interrupts a match.
A written rule for what shape the data must have, used to check it.
A library that checks data against a schema and reports mismatches.
A single recorded event in a match, such as a ball, a wicket or a goal.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Source notes and imports
sections.what: The header explains that this file converts Cricsheet records into events and that the match times are fixed for replays. It brings in the checking library and shared types.
sections.why: The fixed times make replays and tests give the same answer every time.
sections.watch_out: The times shown are replay times, not the moment each ball was bowled.

sections.name: delivery
sections.title: Shape of one ball
sections.what: Describes the fields expected for each ball: the batter, bowler, runs scored, extras and any dismissals. A ball that does not match is rejected.
sections.why: Likely reason: bad source data is caught early instead of producing wrong numbers.
sections.watch_out: If Cricsheet renames a field, every match fails to load.

sections.name: cricsheetMatch
sections.title: Shape of a whole match file
sections.what: Describes the full match: data version, dates, the two teams, season, venue, outcome, and the innings with their overs. Extra fields are allowed.
sections.why: Lets the parser reject malformed files and still accept new fields that Cricsheet adds.
sections.watch_out: The rules require exactly two teams and at least one date, so unusual matches may be rejected.

sections.name: CricsheetMatch
sections.title: Match type and fixed constants
sections.what: Exports the type of a checked match, the source name cricsheet, and the 30-second gap between balls.
sections.why: The source name links this data to its rights record, and the gap is a fixed clock for replays.
sections.watch_out: Changing the source name breaks the link to its rights policy.

sections.name: parseCricsheet, isRainAffected, isTie
sections.title: Turning a match file into events
sections.what: Creates one ball record for each delivery, in order, using the fixed clock. It also builds the competition, the team names, the venue and the outcome. Two helpers mark rain-affected matches and tied matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: the chance calculation must skip matches where the target changed or the result is not a normal win.
sections.watch_out: The rain check only looks for a method field, so any field named method counts as rain.

summary: Turns one Cricsheet match file of ball-by-ball cricket records into a match with one incident per ball.
purpose: It lets the app show cricket matches and ball events, such as wickets and extras, with a traceable source.
why: Cricket data from Cricsheet arrives as nested overs and balls, and the rest of the app needs a flat, checked list of events.
how: It first checks the file's shape using a schema. It then builds a match start time, walks every innings, over and ball in order, and creates one ball incident for each delivery with a fixed 30-second gap. It fills in the teams, venue, competition and outcome, then returns the result. Two small helpers flag rain-affected matches and ties.
inputs: The raw JSON of one Cricsheet match file and its file id, such as 1082591.
outputs: A ParsedEvent with its ball incidents. The helpers return true or false for rain-affected and tied matches.
risks: The match start time and the time for each ball are made up, not real. The file fails completely if any delivery has an unexpected shape.
debug: If a match fails to load, check the error from the schema: it names the field that did not match. Check the Cricsheet format version in the meta data. For wrong timings, check the fixed start time and 30-second spacing.
